key_insight: A hybrid β-VAE-GAN plus sensor-conditioned Transformer can compress and forecast intermittent near-wall turbulence from sparse measurements with physically interpretable latent modes.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a computationally efficient surrogate for wall-bounded CFD, enabling long-horizon flow prediction and reduced-order monitoring with limited sensor input.
method: β-VAE-GAN compresses flow fields into a 4D latent space.
Easy Attention replaces standard self-attention for lower-cost temporal forecasting.
AdaLN-Zero conditions the Transformer on sparse sensor measurements.
evidence_signal: On the Minimal Flow Unit at Reτ = 200 and y+ = 14, the model recovers 87% of turbulent kinetic energy in the latent space and achieves 82% end-to-end reconstruction over forecasts spanning 17,288 t+ from a 128 t+ initialization window.
watch_item: Rare, high-amplitude events are attenuated because the compact latent bottleneck favors the most recurrent flow states.
paper_title: A Hybrid Generative Reduced-Order Model for the Minimal Flow Unit
